h1: NC mandrel benders — pipe, tube and exhaust benders to Ø8-5/8″
intro: An NC mandrel bender is a hydraulic bender whose bend angles are stored in a numeric control: the operator feeds and rotates the tube to a stop — or a servo carrier does it — and the machine bends each angle to the programmed value, with a mandrel inside the tube for thin walls and tight radii. NovoTech sells two makers' NC benders in Canada, all on this page, small to large: ISITAN of Bursa, Turkey — the compact SFB 32 benders for Ø1-1/4″ tube, the SFB 38-NC/A benders for aluminum window and door profiles, the SFB NC/C with a servo-rotation carrier and hydraulic collet for series production and the SFB NC in five sizes from Ø1-1/2″ × 11 ga to Ø3-1/2″ × 8 ga with 100 programs of 20 bends; then CSM of Tainan, Taiwan — the two-head F38 / F50 symmetric benders that bend both ends of a tube at once, the TSRJ / TDRJ with servo feed and rotation and the TNCPB with manual feed to Ø4″, and the single-axis TNCB NC hydraulic pipe benders to Ø8-5/8″. Each family below has its full specification table and photos. The pipe bender most exhaust, handrail, furniture and fabrication shops in Canada actually need — mandrel bending with programmed angles, without the price of a full CNC; CSA-approved panels and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: What is the difference between the SFB NC and the SFB NC/C?
faq.a: On the SFB NC the operator feeds and rotates the tube by hand to the gauge bracket and the NC controls the bend angle. The NC/C adds a carrier with a hydraulic collet and a servo rotation axis: feed to the carrier's adjustable stops, the servo turns the tube to the programmed angle between bends, and the carrier screen shows feed and rotation. For parts with several bends in different planes it is faster and far more repeatable.

An NC bender programs the bend angles; the operator handles feed and rotation (servo rotation on the NC/C, servo feed and rotation on the CSM TSRJ / TDRJ). A CNC bender drives all three axes with servos from a drawing. If you bend hundreds of the same multi-plane part a shift, see our CNC tube benders; for mixed work, exhaust, handrails and furniture, an NC bender pays back faster.

faq.q: What about the mandrel — when do I need it?
faq.a: Thin-wall tube bent to a tight radius (CLR under about 2× the diameter) wrinkles on the inside and flattens on the outside without support. The mandrel supports the tube from inside; every SFB has a hydraulic mandrel and bends with or without it, and a wiper die and ball mandrel are available for the thinnest walls.

faq.q: What do you need from me to quote tooling?
faq.a: Six things: material type, tube or profile size, wall thickness, the smallest centreline radius (CLR) you bend, the maximum bend angle and the maximum tube length. Every bender comes with one die set in the size you request; extra sets, ball mandrels and wiper dies are quoted from the same list.

faq.q: What voltage do the benders run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on the BK-42 and other models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase.
